title_en: Lu County People's Procuratorate, Sichuan Province v. Huang Yi, Yuan Xiaojun, et al. — fraud
ruling_gist_en: Where an actor, for the purpose of illegally obtaining another's property, induces another to participate in gambling by fabricating facts, concealing the truth, or setting traps, and manipulates the outcome of the gambling through fraudulent means to defraud another of property, if the amount involved is relatively large, the act constitutes the crime of fraud and shall be convicted and punished in accordance with Article 266 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

full_text_en:
Luxian County People's Procuratorate of Sichuan Province v. Huang Yi, Yuan Xiaojun, et al. — fraud

【Ruling Summary】

Where an actor, for the purpose of illegally acquiring another person's property, induces another person to participate in gambling by fabricating facts, concealing the truth, or setting a trap, and controls the outcome of the gambling game through fraudulent means, thereby defrauding the victim of property in a relatively large amount, the act constitutes the crime of fraud and shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 266 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Procuratorial Authority: Luxian County People's Procuratorate of Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Huang Yi, male, 43 years old, former Deputy Political Commissar of Xuyong County Public Security Bureau, Sichuan Province, residing at Wulong Residential Community, Shuitangshang, Xuyong Town, Xuyong County; arrested on April 13, 2005.

Defendant: Yuan Xiaojun, male, 37 years old, motor vehicle driver, residing at Zhongxuetang Lane, Xuyong Town, Xuyong County, Sichuan Province; arrested on April 13, 2005.

Defendant: Liu Changmin, male, 33 years old, businessman, residing at Xiaonanhai, Xuyong Town, Xuyong County, Sichuan Province; arrested on April 13, 2005.

Defendant: Liu Xiaodong, male, 37 years old, businessman, residing at Dehou Street, Zhongcheng, Xingwen County, Sichuan Province; arrested on April 13, 2005.

Defendant: Fang Kaiqiang, also known as Fang Wu, male, 35 years old, farmer, residing at Xieziyan Village, Wukuang Town, Jiang'an County, Sichuan Province; arrested on August 9, 2005.

The Luxian County People's Procuratorate of Sichuan Province filed a public prosecution with the Luxian County People's Court of Sichuan Province, charging the defendants Huang Yi, Yuan Xiaojun, Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and Fang Kaiqiang with the crime of fraud.

The indictment alleged: The defendants Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun, in order to repay debts incurred from gambling, conspired to set up a gambling trap and defraud others of money by using marked cards. The two defendants agreed that Huang Yi would select the target victim and Yuan Xiaojun would arrange for persons skilled in using marked cards. Subsequently, Huang Yi contacted the victim Yao Moumou, owner of "Changtian Digital Harbor," falsely claiming that he wanted to discuss matters concerning the purchase and sale of a coal mine with Yao Moumou in person. In the afternoon of November 5, 2004, the defendants Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang arrived in Xuyong County as invited. That evening, Huang Yi, according to the prearranged plan, invited Yao Moumou to dinner together with Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang, and introduced Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang to Yao Moumou as "bosses engaged in the coal business." During the meal, Huang Yi also telephoned the defendants Liu Changmin and Yuan Xiaojun to join the dinner. After dinner, Huang Yi invited the intoxicated Yao Moumou to a teahouse for tea and card games. During the card games, the defendants controlled the outcome through fraudulent means, causing Yao Moumou to lose RMB 580,000. The next day, Huang Yi and others went to "Changtian Digital Harbor" to settle the gambling debt with Yao Moumou. Yao Moumou was forced to offset the gambling debt by converting his two automobiles at a discount of RMB 430,000, together with RMB 140,000 in cash. Huang Yi and the other four defendants then divided the spoils. According to the appraisal by the Jiangyang District Price Certification Center of Luzhou City, the total value of the two vehicles was RMB 416,900. The acts of the five defendants constituted the crime of fraud, and it was requested that the Luxian County People's Court impose punishment according to law.

The defendants Huang Yi, Yuan Xiaojun, Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and Fang Kaiqiang and their defense counsel all argued: The charge brought by the procuratorial authority was improper; the acts of the five defendants did not constitute the crime of fraud but rather the crime of gambling.

The defendant Huang Yi and his defense counsel further argued: While Huang Yi was under "shuanggui" (a form of disciplinary investigation within the Party) by the Luzhou Municipal Commission for Discipline Inspection of the Communist Party of China for other disciplinary violations, he voluntarily and truthfully confessed the criminal facts of this case; therefore, Huang Yi should be deemed to have voluntarily surrendered and be given a lighter punishment according to law.

The defense counsel for the defendant Yuan Xiaojun argued: Yuan Xiaojun provided assistance to the public security organs in arresting the defendant Liu Xiaodong, constituting a meritorious act, and should be given a lighter or mitigated punishment according to law.

The defense counsel for the defendant Liu Changmin argued: Liu Changmin did not participate in the conspiracy beforehand; he played a subsidiary role in the joint crime, was an accomplice, and had performed a meritorious act; therefore, his punishment should be mitigated according to law.

The defense counsel for the defendant Liu Xiaodong argued: Liu Xiaodong was hired by the defendants Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun to participate in gambling; he was in a subordinate position, following instructions and arrangements, played a subsidiary role in the joint crime, was an accomplice, and had performed a meritorious act; therefore, his punishment should be mitigated according to law.

The Luxian County People's Court found through trial:

In October 2004, the defendants Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun, in order to repay debts incurred from gambling, conspired to set up a gambling trap and defraud others of money by using marked cards. The two defendants agreed that Huang Yi would select the target victim and Yuan Xiaojun would arrange for persons skilled in using marked cards. Subsequently, Huang Yi repeatedly telephoned the victim Yao Moumou, owner of "Changtian Digital Harbor," who was conducting business outside, falsely asking Yao Moumou to return home to discuss matters concerning the purchase and sale of a coal mine in person. On November 4, 2004, Yao Moumou returned to Xuyong County from Chengdu. Huang Yi then invited Yao Moumou to have dinner together the next day, while informing Yuan Xiaojun to arrange for persons skilled in using marked cards. In the afternoon of November 5, the defendants Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang arrived in Xuyong County as invited. After testing Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang's skills in using marked cards at the "Guoxiang" Teahouse in Xuyong County seat, Huang Yi expressed satisfaction. Subsequently, according to the prearranged plan, Huang Yi invited Yao Moumou to dinner at the "Shisheng" Hotpot Restaurant in Xuyong County seat that evening. To avoid arousing Yao Moumou's suspicion, Huang Yi introduced Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang to Yao Moumou, falsely claiming that they were "bosses engaged in the coal business." During the meal, Huang Yi also telephoned the defendants Liu Changmin and Yuan Xiaojun to join the dinner. After dinner, at approximately 18:00, Huang Yi invited the intoxicated Yao Moumou to the "Biyulan" Teahouse for tea and card games. First, Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and Yao Moumou played "Dou Dizhu" (a form of gambling) with playing cards. To conceal the scheme, Huang Yi proposed to share a stake with Yao Moumou. During the card game, Liu Xiaodong controlled the high and low cards through fraudulent means, and within just two hours, Yao Moumou lost over RMB 10,000 in cash and incurred debts of over RMB 100,000. Subsequently, Huang Yi and others urged Yao Moumou to switch to "Da Menji" (another form of gambling) in order to win back the money he had lost. Thereafter, Huang Yi, Liu Xiaodong, and Fang Kaiqiang continued to control the card game through fraudulent means. When the card game ended around 23:50, Yao Moumou had lost RMB 580,000, owing RMB 130,000 to Liu Changmin and RMB 440,000 to Fang Kaiqiang. The next day, Yao Moumou invited Huang Yi to his office at "Changtian Digital Harbor," requesting Huang Yi to mediate regarding the gambling debt and asking whether the amount could be reduced. Huang Yi refused Yao Moumou's request, stating that "a gambler must accept the outcome of the game is a rule of gambling," and notified Liu Changmin and Fang Kaiqiang to go to "Changtian Digital Harbor" to settle the gambling debt with Yao Moumou. Yao Moumou was forced to offset the RMB 440,000 debt owed to Fang Kaiqiang by converting his Nissan X-Trail off-road vehicle (license plate Zang 030093) at a discount of RMB 300,000, together with RMB 140,000 in cash, and to offset the RMB 130,000 debt owed to Liu Changmin by converting his Nissan Bluebird sedan (license plate Chuan AET995) at a discount of RMB 130,000. Huang Yi and the other four defendants then drove to a teahouse in the "Dongxiang Hotel" in Xingwen County to divide the spoils. Huang Yi, Yuan Xiaojun, and Liu Changmin each received RMB 30,000; Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang received RMB 50,000; and they agreed to divide the proceeds from the sale of the two vehicles later. According to the appraisal by the Jiangyang District Price Certification Center of Luzhou City, the total value of the two vehicles was RMB 416,900.

It was also found: From March 9 to April 13, 2005, while the defendant Huang Yi was under "shuanggui" by the Luzhou Municipal Commission for Discipline Inspection of the Communist Party of China for other disciplinary violations, before the judicial authorities had learned of the criminal facts of this case and before a criminal case was initiated against him, he voluntarily and truthfully confessed the criminal facts of defrauding the victim Yao Moumou of money by using marked cards together with the other defendants in this case. After the defendant Yuan Xiaojun was brought to justice, he provided information on the whereabouts of the defendant Liu Xiaodong, which assisted the public security organs in arresting Liu Xiaodong. After the defendant Liu Changmin was brought to justice, he provided the public security organs with clues regarding others' crimes of destroying telecommunications facilities and fraud, which were verified as true. After the incident, the vehicles owned by the victim Yao Moumou, the Nissan X-Trail off-road vehicle (license plate Zang 030093) and the Nissan Bluebird sedan (license plate Chuan AET995), were recovered by the public security organs.

The main evidence confirming the above facts includes:

1. Statement of the victim Yao Moumou, the main content being: The defendant Huang Yi telephoned him in October 2004, asking him to return to Xuyong County to discuss coal business. He returned to Xuyong County on November 4, 2004. On the evening of November 5, Huang Yi, under the pretext of welcoming him, invited him to dinner at the "Shisheng" Hotpot Restaurant, introduced him to "Boss Chen and Boss Fang" who were engaged in the coal business, and also notified the defendants Liu Changmin and Yuan Xiaojun to join the meal. After dinner, they went together to the "Biyulan" Teahouse to play cards. That evening, he lost RMB 10,000 in cash and incurred a gambling debt of RMB 570,000. The next day, he asked Huang Yi to mediate in an attempt to have some of the gambling debt reduced, but was refused by Huang Yi. He had no choice but to pay RMB 140,000 in cash and offset RMB 430,000 with two sedans to settle the gambling debt.

2. Testimony of witness Yao Mougang, confirming that on the evening of November 5, 2004, his elder brother Yao Moumou was playing cards at the "Biyulan" Teahouse and asked him to deliver RMB 10,000 in cash. After arriving at the teahouse, he saw Yao Moumou playing cards with two persons, and Huang Yi and others were also present.

3. Testimony of witness Chen Moumou, confirming that at about 12:00 p.m. on November 5, 2004, Yao Moumou called him, saying that he had lost over RMB 500,000 while playing cards with Huang Yi and others. The next day, he went to Yao Moumou's office and saw Yao Moumou settling the gambling debt, with Huang Yi also in the office.

4. Testimony of witness Luo Moumou, confirming that on the evening of November 5, 2004, Yao Moumou and Huang Yi and others ate hotpot at the "Shisheng" Hotpot Restaurant and consumed three bottles of red wine.

5. Testimony of witness Liu Moumou, confirming that on the evening of November 5, 2004, after Yao Moumou, Huang Yi, Liu Changmin, Yuan Xiaojun, and two other men finished dinner at the "Shisheng" Hotpot Restaurant, they went to the "Biyulan" Teahouse for tea and card games.

6. Testimony of witness Huang Moumou, confirming that on the afternoon of November 6, 2004, Yao Moumou asked him to return the sedan and said that the car would be used to offset the gambling debt.

7. Testimony of witnesses Liu Moumou (Yuan Xiaojun's father-in-law) and Liu Moumei (Yuan Xiaojun's wife), confirming that Yuan Xiaojun parked a sedan at his aunt's place and then left.

8. Testimony of witness Zhao Mou, confirming that on March 11, 2005, Liu Changmin drove a sedan and parked it in the parking lot under his management.

9. List of seized items and related documentary evidence, extraction records, photos of stolen goods, and appraisal conclusion of property prices, confirming that the value of Yao Moumou's Nissan X-Trail off-road vehicle (license plate Zang 030093) and Nissan Bluebird sedan (license plate Chuan AET995) totaled RMB 416,900.

10. Record of crime scene inspection, floor plan of the scene, and photos of the scene, confirming that the crime scene was the "Biyulan" Teahouse in Xuyong County.

11. Identification records and photos of each defendant, and permanent residence information forms of each defendant.

12. Acceptance registration form for criminal cases by the public security organs and decision to initiate a criminal investigation.

13. Explanatory notes from the public security organs, confirming that Liu Changmin provided clues regarding others' crimes, which were verified as true; and that Yuan Xiaojun provided relevant clues to assist the public security organs in arresting a co-defendant, the defendant Liu Xiaodong.

14. Explanatory notes from the Luzhou Municipal Commission for Discipline Inspection of the Communist Party of China, confirming that during the period when Huang Yi was under "shuanggui" for other disciplinary violations, he had already voluntarily confessed the fact that he, together with Yuan Xiaojun, Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and the defendant Fang Kaiqiang, defrauded Yao Moumou of money by using marked cards.

15. Confessions and explanations of the defendants Huang Yi, Yuan Xiaojun, Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, Fang Kaiqiang, and others, confirming the fact that the above defendants conspired to set up a gambling trap and win Yao Moumou's money by using marked cards.

16. Audiovisual material of Liu Xiaodong demonstrating his skill in using marked cards, confirming that Liu Xiaodong possessed the skill of using marked cards.

The issue in dispute in this case is: whether the act of the defendants Huang Yi and others in setting up a gambling trap and winning the victim Yao Moumou's money by using marked cards constitutes the crime of fraud or the crime of gambling.

The Luxian County People's Court held:

I. The defendants Huang Yi and others had the subjective intent to commit fraud.

The defendants Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun, because they owed gambling debts, conspired to set up a gambling trap to induce others to participate in gambling, and agreed to control the card game by using marked cards, thereby defrauding others of money. The two made a clear division of labor, with Huang Yi to lure the target victim into gambling and Yuan Xiaojun to contact persons skilled in using marked cards. The defendants Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and Fang Kaiqiang, knowing the intent of Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun, participated in the crime and specifically carried out the fraudulent scheme of controlling the card game by using marked cards, thereby defrauding others of money. In summary, the defendants Huang Yi and others had the subjective intent to illegally acquire others' property through fraudulent means, constituting the intent to commit fraud.

II. The defendants Huang Yi and others objectively carried out fraudulent acts.

Objectively, the defendants Huang Yi and others committed acts of fraud by fabricating facts, concealing the truth, and using deceptive methods to defraud others of property.

First, the defendants Huang Yi and others fabricated the fact of buying and selling a coal mine, and used this as a pretext to contact the victim Yao Moumou, falsely claiming that they needed to discuss the coal mine transaction in person, and subsequently invited Yao Moumou to dinner. After a series of acts to conceal the truth, they ultimately lured Yao Moumou into the pre-arranged gambling trap. Second, Huang Yi and others concealed the true identities of the defendants Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang, falsely introducing them to Yao Moumou as "Boss Chen and Boss Fang," who were bosses engaged in the coal business, thereby gaining Yao Moumou's trust and causing him to mistakenly believe that the meeting with the defendants was to discuss the coal mine transaction, making him unable to detect the gambling trap. Third, during the gambling scheme, to prevent Yao Moumou from detecting the plot, Huang Yi also pretended to share a stake with Yao Moumou, inducing Yao Moumou to participate in gambling without suspicion. Finally, in a genuine gambling activity, the outcome of winning or losing is unpredictable, and the result is uncertain. In this case, during the gambling scheme, the defendants Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and Fang Kaiqiang consistently controlled the outcome of winning or losing through the fraudulent means of using marked cards, resulting in Yao Moumou inevitably losing money, thereby eliminating the uncertainty of the gambling outcome. Therefore, the "gambling" that Huang Yi and others induced Yao Moumou to participate in was no longer genuine gambling, but rather a specific method used by the defendants to commit fraud.

In summary, the acts of the defendants Huang Yi, Yuan Xiaojun, Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and Fang Kaiqiang did not meet the constitutive elements of the crime of gambling. The defense arguments of each defendant and their defense counsel that "the act does not constitute the crime of fraud but constitutes the crime of gambling" cannot be established and are not adopted. Each defendant, with the purpose of illegal possession, by means of fabricating facts and concealing the truth, set up a trap to induce the victim Yao Moumou to participate in gambling, used fraudulent tactics of using marked cards to control the card game during the gambling process, and defrauded Yao Moumou of RMB 150,000 in cash and two sedans, totaling over RMB 560,000, an enormous amount. Their acts have constituted the crime of fraud and shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provisions of Article 266 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Law).

Based on the facts of this case, the defendant Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun conspired to defraud others of money by using marked cards. According to the pre-arranged division of labor, Huang Yi was responsible for selecting the fraud target Yao Moumou, and Yuan Xiaojun was responsible for contacting the defendants Liu Xiaodong and Fang Kaiqiang, who helped with using marked cards. Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun played an organizing and planning role in the joint crime and are both principals. Huang Yi held the position of Deputy Political Commissar of Xuyong County Public Security Bureau, Sichuan Province before the incident, had the status of a law enforcement officer, and played a primary organizing and directing role throughout the criminal process; his status and role in the joint crime were greater than that of Yuan Xiaojun, who is also a principal. The defendants Liu Changmin, Liu Xiaodong, and Fang Kaiqiang knew of Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun's fraudulent criminal intent before specifically carrying out the crime, had formed a conspiracy subjectively, and had a joint criminal intent to commit fraud. As the implementers of the specific crime, these three defendants played a secondary role in this case and are all accomplices, and shall be given a lighter or mitigated punishment according to law. The defense arguments of the defense counsel for Liu Changmin and Liu Xiaodong in this regard are established and are adopted. Huang Yi voluntarily and truthfully confessed the fraudulent criminal facts of this case before the public security organs had learned of the criminal facts of this case and before a criminal case was initiated against him, which may be deemed as voluntary surrender. The defense argument of his defense counsel in this regard is established and is adopted. After Yuan Xiaojun was brought to justice, he provided the whereabouts of the co-defendant Liu Xiaodong, which assisted the public security organs in arresting Liu Xiaodong, which may be deemed as a meritorious act. The defense argument of his defense counsel in this regard is established and is adopted. After Liu Changmin was brought to justice, he provided clues regarding others' crimes, which were verified as true, and he has a meritorious act. The defense argument of his defense counsel in this regard is established and is adopted. Taking into account the facts and circumstances of this case, combined with the fact that stolen goods such as vehicles have been recovered, all five defendants, including Huang Yi and Yuan Xiaojun, may be given a mitigated punishment according to law.

Accordingly, in accordance with the provisions of Article 266, Article 52, Article 53, Paragraph 1 of Article 25, Paragraphs 1 and 4 of Article 26, Article 27, Paragraph 1 of Article 67, and Paragraph 1 of Article 68 of the Criminal Law, the Luxian County People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 19, 2006:

I. The defendant Huang Yi is guilty of fraud and is sentenced to eight years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000;

II. The defendant Yuan Xiaojun is guilty of fraud and is sentenced to seven years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000;

III. The defendant Liu Xiaodong is guilty of fraud and is sentenced to seven years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000;

IV. The defendant Fang Kaiqiang is guilty of fraud and is sentenced to seven years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000;

V. The defendant Liu Changmin is guilty of fraud and is sentenced to six years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 40,000.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, none of the defendants appealed within the statutory period, and the procuratorial authority did not file a protest. The judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
